validated_results.title: Lifestyle and prostate cancer among older African-American and Caucasian men in South Carolina.
validated_results.reason: This population-based case-control study evaluated the association between dietary lycopene intake and incident prostate cancer risk.

sample_size.excerpt: After eliminating 59 subjects (7 cases and 52 controls) who had prevalent prostate cancer and three subjects (2 cases and 1 control) who completed fewer than five questions, the final sample size was 845 subjects (416 cases, 429 controls). Of those, 11 cases and 36 controls completed questions on age, race, education, cancer history, history of benign prostatic hyperplasia, and prostate-specific antigen and digital rectal exam screening only, resulting in 407 cases and 393 controls for most analyses.
sample_size.location: Materials and methods, paragraph 3; total_n derived from reported group counts 407 + 393 = 800

design.excerpt: This population-based case–control study was conducted in South Carolina from 2000 to 2002.

timing.excerpt: Although none of the men indicated their diet had changed since the reference date, they were asked to recall their diet for the period immediately prior to the reference date.

continent.excerpt: This population-based case–control study of prostate cancer among men aged 65–79 years was conducted between 2000 and 2002 in South Carolina.

exposure_measurement.excerpt: Diet was assessed in a 20-item food frequency questionnaire and pertained to foods consumed at least once a year.

extraction.p_value_method: two-sided Wald test from effect and 95% CI on the log scale
